question: Who, according to Stesichorus, was given a bow by Apollo to fight off his unearthly pursuers, although in a more famous version the deciding vote by Athena acquitted him of murdering Clytemnestra?
According to Euripides, what city was the site of Orestes’s trial, as well as Myscelus’s trial in Ovid?
After the trial on the Areopagus, under what name were the furies worshipped in a cave at Athens?
Pausanias saw an example of what object hanging by ribbons from a temple roof at Sparta, while another, in an event commemorated by the constellation Pisces, was rolled out of the Euphrates by fish?
The first egg is Helen’s. In some accounts, what deity was her mother after mating with Zeus?
Aphrodite, the inhabitant of the second egg, was supposedly called what epithet by the Assyrians?
Whose death may have resulted from challenging Artemis to a discus match, an unintentional shot from a distant Artemis, or being Eos’ lover, although most famously a scorpion sent by Gaia killed him?
In one account, who tricked Artemis into shooting Orion, fearing that she would marry the hunter?
In some accounts Orion can walk on water, but what other ability may have let him cross the sea?

Who spat in his teacher’s mouth to forget the art of prophecy after a snake couple showed how he could be revived, since Polyidus had found him drowned in a honey-jar to the shock of his father Minos?
What son of Apollo and Evadne, a future great seer, was not killed by honey, but rather saved by it, since snakes fed it to him after he was abandoned on Aepytus’s orders?
Honey was also the diet of a set of three-winged prophetesses mentioned in the Homeric Hymn to Hermes. These are likely to be identified with what group, who practiced divination with pebbles?
What sort of object, which Gelonus, unlike one of his brothers, failed to use, was given to Poeas on Mount Oeta, and then to Poeas’s son, shortly after it was used to kill Nessus with Hydra venom?
Gelonus and Agathyrsus were two of the three children Heracles had with a half-snake woman in a forest. What brother of theirs successfully used Heracles’s bow?
Some say Poeas had earlier used a different bow to shoot what man — if he can be called that — in his vulnerable ankle?
What pair of brothers, who led 30 ships to Troy from Tricca, used herbs from Chiron to take care of Philoctetes and Menelaus, just as their father Asclepius would have?
In what region, where Nestor grew up, were Machaon’s bones buried?
Podaleirius managed to survive the Trojan War and settled down. What mysterious feature did the Delphic Oracle tell him to look for when choosing a place to settle?
answer: A place where the sky would not harm him if it fell

question: The efforts of her close friend Acca, Diana’s devotee Opis, and her father throwing her across the Amasenus, were all intended to prevent the death of what daughter of Metabus and queen of the Volsci?
What Trojan ally dealt the fatal blow to Camilla and was killed himself shortly thereafter by Opis?
As she whirled across the battlefield, Camilla fixated on a potential victim named Chloreus who was distinctive in what way? A general description is acceptable.
Perhaps born alongside mountain-nymphs and Satyrs as grandsons of Hecaterus, what beings stole Epaphus and were killed by Zeus, though the din of their shields had saved him in infancy?
A different tribe of human Curetes are most known in mythology for their quarrel with what neighboring people, whose kings included Porthaon, Andraemon, and Agrius?
The discovery of what lost prince was perhaps made possible through the divination of the divine Curetes?
What two men hid in an oak tree but were seen all the way from Mount Taygetus via superhuman sight, allowing their cousins to avenge the seizure of Leucippus’s daughters Phoebe and Hilaeira?
According to another version, what woman was so distraught at learning that the Dioscuri had killed the sons of Aphareus — one of whom was her husband — that she committed suicide?

Pausanias points out that, following a genealogy reported by the Cypria, Marpessa’s daughter and granddaughter also committed suicide upon the deaths of their husbands. Name both of these women. One was married to an Aetolian hero, the other to a soldier at Troy.
answer: Cleopatra (Wife of Meleager) and Polydora (Wife of Protesilaus)

question: What profession was first practiced by the Chalybes, held by a man who rented a lot to the Spartan Lichas, and for nine years was performed for Eurynome’s benefit by the divine father of Ericthonius?
What was the profession of Damarmenus, who returned a sacred body part to the Eleians?
What was the name of the goatherd who found, then turned away from, a baby with lightning flashing around him?
In Ovid’s Metamorphoses, what city sees Iris lead its queen to the comet that deifies her, a spear transform into a willow tree, and a snake slither off a ship bringing the cult of Aesculapius?
The transformation of Romulus’s spear into a willow tree is related after a description of the birth of what Etruscan teacher of divination from a clod of dirt?
The amazement of Romulus at the willow tree and of an Etruscan herdsman at Tages’s birth is also said to be analogous to what man’s amazement upon seeing his reflection in a nearby river?
What deity, worshiped above all others in Megalopolis, was denied an Athenian bride because Tereus had made them anti-Thracian, leading him to come to the Ilissus river and snatch Oreithyia away?
Pandion had initially sought Tereus’s help in a boundary war with what other ruler, according to Apollodorus?
What Dardanian king owned three thousand horses, which were so splendid that Boreas took the form of a stallion to mate with them?
What name is shared by a vicious son of Ares killed near Itonus by Heracles, a king of Colonae who was invulnerable but was still strangled by Achilles, and a Ligurian king who mourned Phaethon?
Apollo blotted out the first Cycnus’s grave by redirecting what river, the same one which had caused Jason to lose his sandal?
The second Cycnus was implicated in the classic mythological trope where his second wife accused his son of rape. Name this second wife.
Watched in the sky by Arctos, followed threateningly by Scorpio, and accompanied by Canis Major, what constellation exemplifies its namesake’s myths — though not his blinding by Oenopion?
What deity sent a scorpion to kill Orion for his boast that he could hunt every animal?
When Orion was blinded, he lifted what man onto his shoulders and ordered him to guide him eastward toward Helios?
In the Aeneid, who describes killing Feronia’s son Erylus before showing the sites of the Argiletum, Lupercal and Janiculum to Aeneas and telling the story of how Hercules killed Cacus?
Evander also claims that he had been sent a crown by what Etruscan king, begging him for military assistance against Mezentius?
Evander also describes what horrendous form of torture performed by Mezentius?
What demi-god, the son of Saturn and Venilia, was the grandfather of Latinus?
What god was Venilia's father?
What happened to Picus when he rejected the advances of Circe?
answer: She turned him into a woodpecker

question: Amycus, Io, Aegialeus, and Phoroneus were all children of what sort of beings, the sisters of the Erinyes and the Giants?
What river god was the father of Aegialeus, Phoroneus, and Io?
What god was the father of Amycus?
What name is shared by the first son of Zeus and a mortal woman, the eldest son of Phrixus, and the son of Arestor who killed Echidna?
What name is shared with the mother of Argus who was the first mortal seduced by Zeus, and the mother of Chloris and Amyclas?
What daughter of Aeetes was Argus' mother and Phrixus' wife?
What Greek physician settled in the Carian Cheronese after the Trojan War due to a prophecy by the Delphic Oracle?
What was the prophecy?
answer: Settle where the sky would not harm him if it fell

question: What led Podaleirius to believe that the Cheronese was his prophesied new home?
answer: It was surrounded by high mountains

question: In the Iliad, elm trees were planted around the burial mound of what king, who ruled a city at the foot of Mt. Placus, and, after being killed alongside his 7 sons, was buried in full armor by Achilles?
What was the apt name of Eetion’s city that he ruled?
During another of Achilles’ excursions, he captures what son of Priam, while he worked in an orchard, and sold him and his brothers Isus and Antiphus for ransom?
What event, where judges wore dark-coloured clothing in mourning, rewarded victors with parsley, and was founded by Adrastus to honor an infant nicknamed Archemorus?
Right after these games, the Seven Against Thebes reached Thebes where Tydeus met what man, who was sent alongside Polyphontes and 50 other men to challenge him?
Who was the father of the 4 leading defenders of Thebes, most notably Melanippus, whose brains were eaten?

After he dreamt that a woman asked him to give her a home at Anaphe, who threw the Triton-given gift of a clod of earth into the sea, then returned home with the Argonauts he had once saved with a dove?
Euphemus was originally from what town at the tip of the Peloponnesus, which was celebrated as an entrance to the Underworld?
What Spartan leader led Euphemus’ descendants to the island Calliste, which he later renamed after himself?
What sort of ritual caused a feud between Mastusius and Demophon, saved Athens from Eurystheus’ forces with Macaria’s help, and nearly occurred at Aulis to produce winds?
What king of Athens sacrificed one of his daughters after an oracle said it was necessary to defeat the forces of Eleusis?
What Locrian man stopped an annual human sacrifice in the town of Temesa by beating a ghostly hero in a boxing-match?
12 days after he was returned to Troy from custody by Eëtion of Imbros, what son of Laothoë was killed by Achilles, who had once seized him in the orchard of his father Priam?
Laothoë was also said to be the mother of what son of Priam, often called his youngest?
Achilles had captured Lycaon while he was harvesting tree shoots in Priam’s orchard. Name either the type of tree that he was using or what he was making with them.
In the Aeneid, Orodes prophesies the death of what man — the rider of the horse Rhaebus and the ruler of Caere — before he duels Aeneas in the hopes of avenging Lausus’ death?
What king of the Etruscans fought alongside Aeneas out of hatred for Mezentius?
According to one story, a man named Tarchon uncovered what autochthonous Etruscan prophet while plowing?
What mountain’s crag of Coddinus was carved with an old image of Cybele by Broteas, whose sister turned to stone on it when she could not stop weeping for her slain children?
Which of Niobe’s children survived the killing of her siblings and was renamed when she became permanently pale with fear during the killing?
According to one story, Zeus threw Mount Sipylus on Tantalus when Tantalus abetted what man’s theft of a guard-dog from Zeus’ shrine on Crete?
What island housed a magical garden in which fruit never died, ships that guided themselves without oarsmen, and gold and silver watch-dogs that guarded the palace of Alcinous?
Scheria also housed Medea’s cave, which had originally been home to what woman?
What goddess, who was indirectly referenced by the island’s original name “Drepane”, brought wealth to the island out of fondness for Macris?
What name in mythology is shared among a king set adrift in a chest that landed at Oenoe, a son of Andraemon who led 40 ships to Troy, and a king who tried to kill Orestes at Tauria?
What descendant of the Aetolian king Thoas later took over the throne of Elis from Dius and invited Agorius to share power with him?
What son did Odysseus bear to an unnamed daughter of Thoas son of Andraemon?
What son of Alxion had one child who pretended to be a woman to reach Daphne and a daughter who murdered her bastard son Chrysippus, both of whom eclipse his deeds as king of Pisa?
Identify one figure who is commonly named as Oenomaus’ mother.
Pelops was not the first to compete for Hippodameia’s hand, and Pausanias conveniently gives us all the names of her previous suitors, who all lost the chariot race. Name one of them.
answer: ONE OF: MARMAX / ALCATH(O)US / EURYALUS / EURYMACHUS / CROTALUS / ACRIAS / CAPETUS / LYCURGUS / LASIUS / CHALCODON / TRICOLONUS / ARISTOMACHUS / PRIAS / PELAGON / AEOLIUS / CRONIUS / ERYTHRAS / EIONEUS

question: No flute player could enter the sanctuary of what man, who was accused of making advances on his stepmother Philonome and sent by his father Cycnus to an island near Troy that soon took his name?
Who was the sister of Tenes that, for some reason, was also shipped along with him?
Who was the flute player that bore false witness to Philonome’s accusations, and was stoned to death by Cycnus?
In the Iliad, who vowed to sacrifice a hundred lambs before striking a dove to win the archery contest at Patroclus’ funeral games, after which he returned to his homeland Crete alongside Idomeneus?
What item from Eleon did Meriones give to Odysseus, which was originally stolen by Odysseus’ grandfather Autolycus?
Meriones was responsible for some of the most cruel wounds in the Iliad. Who was the builder of Paris’ ship who was struck in the right buttock?
What island — home to Hyllus’s mother, Melite — served as the refuge of a Euboean woman who had nursed Dionysus and the adopted homeland of natives of Hypereia who were led by Nausithous?
answer: One of SCHERIA / DREPANE / PHAEACIA / CORFU

question: Nausithous led the Phaeacians from Hypereia since they were being harassed by what neighbors?
What son of Nausithous died to Apollo on the day of his wedding?
Who won his kingdom after defeating the invading Idas, was suckled by a doe and named for the animal, and seized the infant Orestes to force the Greeks to heal a wound from Achilles’ spear?
Telephus originally had come to Teuthrania in search of what woman, his mother?
What king’s shepherds found the infant Telephus on Mount Parthenius and gave him his name?
What deity was supposed to be the heir to Zeus until he was distracted with toys and carried away, afterwhich Athena could only rescue his heart from the Titans who had torn him into pieces?
Who was abandoned by his mother because she feared her father Crotopus, and was eventually shredded to pieces by dogs?
In order to overtake Arcadia, Pelops pretended friendship with what king, whom he haddismembered and scattered his limbs across the land?
What daughters of Achelous may have been attendants of Persephone, resided on the island of Anthemoessa, and forced Odysseus’s men to use wax to not be drowned by their deadly song?
Which Argonaut drowned out the sirens with his lyre-playing?
What Argonaut was nevertheless almost killed, but was saved by Aphrodite and fathered Eryx?
Four Athenian girls sacrificed themselves to stop what sort of event, which occurred in Troy after Laomedon’s refusal to pay Apollo, and afflicted the Greek camp at Troy after Chryseis’s abduction?
What Boeotian city suffered a plague due to its former king’s murder?
What family’s invasion of Greece was halted by a plague, leading to the Delphic Oracle prophesying their success in “the third crop”?
What kind of object, a famous one of which was made by Tychius out of seven cowhides, depicted scenes such as a city at peace and at war and the constellations on one made for Achilles by Hephaestus?
What Greek at Troy wielded the first shield referenced, and often used it to protect his half-brother as he shot arrows at the Trojans?
What man’s shield depicted scenes from Roman history such as the battle of Actium?
Balancing water jars was a feature of what sort of event on Aegina, though more famous examples of these contests are the ones won by Odysseus to marry Penelope and Melanion for the hand of Atalanta?
After Odysseus won his footrace, he was exhorted by Icarius to stay in what martial city?
As Icarius pursued the newlyweds, Penelope was told to either stay willingly or return to her father.What action did she take to signal to Icarius that she would be leaving?
answer: Covered her head with a veil

question: What inanimate objects were a couple who called each other Zeus and Hera, Rhodope and Haemus, turned into, and include Chiron’s home, Pelion, which was stacked by the Aloadae to reach Olympus?
After the great flood, Deucalion’s boat ran aground at what mountain, which was said to be one ofthe favored homes of the Muses?
The form of a hawk was given to what man after he flung himself from the slopes of Parnassus indespair over his daughter Chione’s death?
What activity was excelled at by figures such as Mecisteus, his son Euryalus, Entellus, Dares, and Eryx,and was used to defeat the Bebrycian king Amycus by Pollux?
What contest at Patroclus’ funeral game was surprisingly won by Meriones, who defeated Teucer?
What activity did Achilles give Agamemnon the first prize in without holding a contest?
What sort of animal did Zeus turn into to lie with Persephone and father Zagreus, were Cadmus and Harmonia transformed into at their deaths, and did Heracles strangle as a baby in his crib?
Other snakes in mythology include what hundred-headed serpent honored by the constellation Draco?
What archer was driven into exile due to the foul odor emitted from a wound he received via snakebite?
What group took shelter at Malea after being driven out of Thessaly in the aftermath of a drunken battle at a wedding, where one of these creatures, Eurytion, attempted to kidnap Hippodameia?
What hero had driven the Centaurs to Mount Pholoe after they had tried to steal his host’s wine?
The centaurs may have been invited to Peirithous’ wedding due to their common descent from what man?
What son of Iphiclus was brought back from the dead to see his lamenting wife Laodameia one last time after his life was cut short by Hector when he landed first among the Greeks at Troy?
When he died, what brother of his led the contingent in his place? This brother shares his name with Priam before Priam was ransomed.
Protesilaus and Podarces’s father Iphiclus had actually been cured of impotence by what seer, who saved his own life by overhearing some woodworms
What god, who punished the nymph Telphusa for tricking him, joined Hermes in raping Chione and killed the Cyclopes out of anger to avenge his son Asclepius, the healing god?
Why had Apollo killed the Cyclopes specifically to avenge his son Asclepius?
Why had Zeus killed Asclepius in the first place?

Who was wounded by Euphorbus after Apollo struck the helmet from his head, before being killed by Hector, a sad end to a warrior who had earlier killed Sarpedon and borrowed his lover Achilles’ armor?
What action had Partroclus been prevented from performing thrice by Apollo?
The philosopher Pythagoras claimed to be Euphorbus’ reincarnation, and could remember his past lives due to also being what Argonaut, a son of Hermes?
What profession was shared by Damarmenus, who found Pelops’s shoulder bone; a man who ate an herb and became a god named Glaucus; and Dictys, who took care of Perseus after catching him in his net?
Pelops’ shoulder bone was lost while returning from what place, where it was prophesied to help win a war?
What son of Priam had made this prophecy after the Greeks captured him?

What port city, where an omen involving eight chicks and their mother was interpreted by Calchas, saw it falsely claimed that Achilles was to marry there when still winds forced the sacrifice of Iphigenia?
In many versions, Iphigenia did not die, but was snatched away and carried off to what people?
Some say that Iphigenia was not a biological child of Agamemnon and Clytemnestra, but was instead a daughter of Helen and what man, who had taken her to Aphidnae in Attica?
Who sacrificed to Onca but was soon forced to serve a “great year” under Ares for killing a dragon whose teeth created the Spartoi that would populate his new city of Thebes?
The Phoenician goddess Onca is commonly identified with what other deity, who directed Cadmus to draw the dragon’s teeth and sow half of them?
The other half of the dragon’s teeth were given by Athena to what king?
In Book 11 of the Metamorphoses, what unfortunate woman sees Morpheus in a dream, where she learns of her husband’s death by shipwreck shortly before their transformation into kingfishers?
According to Ovid, Alcyone — like Sisyphus — is the offspring of what god, a son of Hippotas whom Ovid conflates with a son of Hellen with two Ls?
An old man’s observation of kingfishers serves as the segue into the story of what son of Priam who was transformed into a diver-bird?
Pushed off the cliffs of Scyros by Lycomedes, what man faced Amazons on the Areopagus, tried to kidnap Persephone along with Pirithous, and defeated brigands on his way from Troezen to Athens?
Who was responsible for Theseus almost drinking aconite until Aegeus recognized him?
What demagogue stirred up resentment against Theseus and replaced him while he was in the Underworld trying to kidnap Persephone, causing him to make that journey to Scyros?
What two men, one a son of Hippolochus and the other a son of Tydeus, met in battle at Troy and, after learning that their grandfathers were friends, exchanged armor?
Respectively, who were the grandfathers of Diomedes and Glaucus that knew each other?
Diomedes had initially asked Glaucus who he was to avoid accidentally provoking a god; he cites the story of what foolish king who pursued Dionysus’s nurses with ox-goads?
Odysseus received a silver mixing bowl, 7 talents of gold, and 12 jars of strong red wine from what priest of Apollo at Ismarus — a gift that came in useful when he confronted Polyphemus?
Ismarus is part of what larger region of Greece, which also housed the mares of Diomedes and Pierus’s son Oeagrus?
Polyphemus had been warned of Odysseus by what seer, a son of Eurymus?

Identify and correct the error here: After Zeus prolonged the night to sleep with Alcmene in disguise as Amphitryon, Heracles was born alongside Iolaus, whom he saved by strangling twin serpents as a baby.

Now identify and correct the error here: During events related to the Trojan War, Aeneas was chased down from Mount Eryx by Achilles, had his hip crushed by a rock thrown by Diomedes, and was saved by Poseidon.
Now identify and correct the error here: Telethusa wanted to save her daughter Cleopatra from her husband Ligdus killing her, so she prayed to Isis to transform her into a boy.
What woman gave the name byrsa to her city’s citadel after she bought the land from Iarbas, whom she refused to marry out of grief for Sychaeus even as she was inflamed with love for Aeneas?
After Dido committed suicide, who was sent to free Dido’s soul from her body, which she did by cutting a lock of Dido’s golden hair?
According to the Aeneid, Dido’s father had what name, though he is seemingly not the same person as the son of Poseidon and Libya and twin brother of Agenor?
What sort of animal, into which Polydorus’s mother was transformed after avenging him, was exemplified in myth by Maera, Laelaps, Argus on Ithaca, and Cerberus?
What man received from his wife both Laelaps and a javelin that could never fail? He used Laelaps to hunt the Teumessian Vixen but the javelin to accidentally kill his wife.
Maera was owned by what father-daughter pair, one of whom tried to teach the Athenians about wine?
What man slaughtered the Greek flocks in a bout of madness, then committed suicide near Troy after being denied the arms of Achilles, meaning he could not return home to Salamis?
According to Ovid, Ajax’s name was alluded to by the letters “AI AI” which appeared on what flower, which blossomed out of his blood following his suicide?
Ajax’s name is also said to refer to what animal, which appeared to his father Telamon as an indication that he would be a great warrior?
The Cians annually wandered their land crying the name of what boy, who was taken in Mysia by the nymph of the spring Pegae while Heracles was fixing his oar to rejoin the Argonauts?
What fellow Argonaut helped Heracles look for Hylas? He shares his name with a figure who tried to woo Galatea with his pipe-playing and killed her lover Acis.
The Argonauts actually left Heracles behind at the insistence of what two men?
What deity came to the Ilissus river to abduct the dancing girl Oreithyia, then fathered Phineus’s saviors — the Argonauts Zetes and Calais, whose graves swayed when his North wind blew on them?
What sister of Oreithyia and daughter of Erechtheus fled to Crete at one point during her life, where Minos gave her the hunting dog Laelaps?
Boreas and Oreithyia were also the parents of what wife of Phineus?
What woman, spotted hiding near Vesta’s temple in a possibly spurious passage of the Aeneid, married Deiphobus and imitated the voices of Greeks’ wives before being reunited with Menelaus?
After Paris died, Deiphobus competed with what prophet brother of his for Helen’s hand?
Helen may have been the mother of Iphigeneia by what man, who kidnapped her as a child?
What mythological group, which Apollo made drunk to help his friend, convinced Typhon to eat weakening fruit, told Althaea about a magical log, and included Clotho and Atropos?
Who was Apollo’s friend, a king of Pherae who also hosted Heracles and called on the god’s assistance in yoking a lion and boar to his chariot?
Name one of the two Giants that the Fates killed in battle.
What kind of animal, born from Theophane, appeared at Orchomenus to foil Ino’s plans when Nephele called it to carry her children Phrixus and Helle to Colchis, where its fleece was hung up?
What Greek god created the constellation Aries after a ram led him to water in the Libyan desert, shortly before he went on a longer expedition that took him to the Ganges river?
In addition to immortalizing the constellation, to what ram-headed Libyan god, identified with Zeus and said by Vergil to be the father of Iarbas, did Dionysus establish a shrine?
Ultimately dying at the spring Telphusa, what man advised Liriope when she asked about Narcissus, then gave prophecies to Cadmus, Oedipus, and other Thebans despite his blindness?
Tiresias died after Thebes was sacked by what group, whose name means “Offspring,” since they finished the job started by their parents?
Who was Tiresias’s mother, a favorite companion of Athena who was present when Tiresias saw the goddess naked?
What king married a daughter of Catreus named Aerope, whose actions eventually led him to feed his nephews to his brother Thyestes and send the young Agamemnon and Menelaus away for safety?
During their contest for the rule of Mycenae, Thyestes offered that the throne should go to the one who could produce what object, knowing that Aerope had secretly given it to him
What other son of Pelops and Hippodameia founded a city in honor of his eponymous brother and had his daughter briefly courted by Bellerophon?
What sort of animal appeared to Telamon outside Troy, stole Aphrodite’s sandal, caused Hebe to be replaced by carrying Ganymede to Olympus, and pecked at the liver of Prometheus every day?
Heracles freed Prometheus from the eagle shortly after leading a search for what man alongside the Lapith Polyphemus?
Heracles freed Prometheus from the eagle shortly after leading a search for what man alongside the Lapith Polyphemus?
Betrothed to one of Ascanius’s victims, Numanus Remulus, what woman tricks Tolumnius into restarting battle and takes the form of Metiscus in order to help her Rutulian brother Turnus?
What deity awarded Juturna with immortality and the control of springs and waters after raping her?
Juturna’s name may be a compound of Turnus and a root shared with what Latin verb?
After sacking Teleutas’s city, what Greek warrior took Tecmessa as his concubine, then left her grieving when he committed suicide on Hector’s sword over not winning the arms of Achilles?
Although Ajax came from the island of Salamis, his brother Teucer founded a city called Salamis on what other island, the home of Paphos and Pygmalion?
Name the son that Tecmessa bore to Ajax, whom Ajax named after his famous broad shield.
Sailing in Noëmon’s ship, what man transported the seer Theoclymenus with him after Athena — who often appeared disguised as Mentor — told him to return from Pylos and go back to Penelope?
What son of Nestor accompanied Telemachus for much of his journey?
During his journey, Telemachus learns that what woman was taught magic by Polydamna?
What hero competed in games hosted by Teutamides shortly before making an agreement with Proetus’ son Megapenthes to trade kingdoms, since he was ashamed to inherit Argos by killing Acrisius?
What other important city did Perseus found, employing the Cyclopes to build walls for him just as they had done for Tiryns?
Acrisius and Proetus were known for feuding in the womb, but who was the father of these troublesome tykes?
In the Iliad, what deity takes the form of a chalcis bird shortly after winning Pasithea as a bride, works with Thanatos to carry off the corpse of Sarpedon, and puts both gods and men to sleep?
Hypnos’s bride Pasithea was the youngest of what group of mythological sisters?
On what island, the home of the Sintians, did Hera convince Hypnos to lull Zeus to sleep?
Though he became a lion, snake, and tree, what deity’s daughter Eidothea explained in Book 4 of the Odyssey how Menelaus could restrain him when he emerged from the sea?
What man similarly captured Nereus to get important information shortly before tricking Atlas?
Who was similarly taught how to capture Proteus by his mother Cyrene?
Criticizing the treatment of Palamedes and feigning anger at Ulysses’s cruelty, who deceptively earned the trust of Priam and persuaded him to accept a wooden horse with the city walls?
Sinon’s story was believable partly because Ulysses did actually have a grudge against Palamedes in mythology. What had Palamedes done to provoke this anger?
answer: Palamedes put baby Telemachus in front of a "crazed" Odysseus' plough to prove Odysseus was sane

question: What son of Thestor, who had predicted from seeing a snake and some sparrows that the Trojan War would last ten years, supposedly helped Ulysses try to kill Sinon?
What sort of animal, whose blood killed Aeson and whose scary emergence from the sea near Athens killed Hippolytus, was built out of wood by Daedalus to help Pasiphae fulfill her love?
What son of Minos was killed by a bull?
What Theban woman gave her name to a spring near Thebes after being dragged along by a bull?
